 Probabilmente acquistato nel 1968 presso Tiffany & Co. a New York, questo orologio fu scelto da Joanne Woodward come regalo per il marito Paul Newman, proprio all’inizio della sua passione per il motorsport. Per rendere il dono ancora più speciale, Joanne fece incidere sul fondello il celebre messaggio: “DRIVE CAREFULLY ME” (guida con prudenza - me).  L’orologio è stato venduto nel 2017, durante l’asta Winning Icons di Phillips, per la strabiliante cifra di $17.752.500.

On this day in 1991, Eastern Air Lines, one of America’s most iconic airlines, was dissolved after 64 years, ending a name that once felt baked into the fabric of U.S. travel. For decades, Eastern was a familiar sight up and down the East Coast, a major player in Florida and the Caribbean, and a carrier many travelers simply grew up with.

What happened: after years of financial chaos and labor conflict, the airline’s remaining operations unraveled and the company was dissolved, leaving employees and loyal flyers watching a giant disappear in real time. It was a brutal reminder that even the biggest, most recognizable airline brands can run out of runway.

What came next: Eastern’s remaining pieces didn’t vanish, they were absorbed. Many assets were parceled out to other carriers, including American and Continental, as the industry reshuffled routes and airport space. In the months that followed, the map of who flew where shifted, and Eastern’s footprint became part of other airlines’ growth stories. See more history at BrookeInTheAirTravel.squarespace.com

A história de Dan Saunders parece até roteiro de filme, mas aconteceu de verdade. Em 2011, o bartender australiano descobriu por acaso uma falha nos caixas eletrônicos do National Australia Bank. Durante a madrugada, quando os terminais ficavam offline, ele conseguia transferir valores inexistentes entre suas próprias contas e sacar dinheiro que simplesmente não existia no sistema.

🍾 Com o “glitch”, Dan mergulhou em meses de luxo improvável. Viajou em jatos particulares, bancou festas caras, hospedou-se em hotéis de alto padrão e pagou despesas de amigos como se tivesse feito fortuna da noite para o dia. Ele dizia que havia movimentado cerca de 1,6 milhão de dólares australianos, embora documentos posteriores indicassem valores bem menores.

⚖️ Aos poucos, a culpa e o medo começaram a pesar. Mesmo gastando livremente, Dan sabia que tudo aquilo tinha prazo de validade. Quando a falha começou a ser investigada, ele tomou a decisão que mudaria tudo: procurou a imprensa, contou toda a história e se entregou à polícia. Foi condenado, obrigado a ressarcir parte dos valores e cumpriu pena.

🔄 Após a repercussão internacional, Dan abandonou a vida de excessos e tentou recomeçar longe dos holofotes. Voltou ao trabalho comum e passou a refletir sobre como um erro bancário transformou sua vida de forma tão rápida quanto temporária.

Brazil’s Oil Boom: From Pre-Salt to Powerhouse.

Brazil is flexing its energy muscles, leading Latin America’s oil resurgence with ambitions as bold as its samba beats. By 2030, the country aims to pump out a staggering 5.3 million barrels of crude oil daily, a 40% leap from 2025 levels. This surge is fueled by its prolific pre-salt fields, where Petrobras, the state-controlled oil giant, is investing $109 billion to tap into reserves that are 84% crude oil. With breakeven costs as low as $28 per barrel, Brazil’s light, sweet crude is a hot commodity, especially as global supply disruptions make its oil indispensable to markets like China and the U.S. In January 2026 alone, Brazil produced nearly 4 million barrels per day, a 14.6% increase year-over-year, solidifying its position as a top contender to overtake Canada as the world’s fourth-largest oil producer.

WWF-Brazil and the International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) argue that 85% of Brazil’s planned oil extraction would be unprofitable if the world meets its 1.5°C climate target. Environmentalists, including scientists mapping the Amazon Reef, have slammed President Lula’s approval of exploratory drilling near this fragile ecosystem, calling it a betrayal of Brazil’s climate commitments. Investors worry about Petrobras’ rising debt and shrinking dividends, questioning whether oil wealth will truly trickle down to Brazil’s poorest communities. Petrobras ($PBR) and global players like Shell ($SHEL) are cashing in, making Brazil a focal point for energy investors.
